texts.li: [food] {A_nameDef} came back from a walk with stained fingers. Patches of wild {TALE} have ripened all over the colony's land, by the paths and along the edges of the fields, and they won't keep forever.

[medicine] There's {TALE} coming up all across the colony's land this season, far more than usual, and {A_nameDef} has marked where. Cut and dried, it would keep the healer's shelf stocked for a good while.
[food] {A_nameDef} ate half of what {A_pronoun} picked on the way back, which is how the colony found out. There are patches of wild {TALE} ripe all over its land, and more coming.

There's a comet over the colony, a long pale smear across the sky, bright enough to see by day. It will hang there for several days. Work keeps stopping while people look up at it, and the arguments over what it means go on late into the night.

[lowtech] A star with a tail has appeared in the sky. The old folk have stories about such things, and the stories don't agree. It's a sign of good harvests, or of war, or of a king's death, depending on who tells it. It will hang there for days.

[!lowtech] A bright comet is passing close enough to see by day. One of the colonists worked out its orbit and says it won't be back for nine hundred years. Opinion is split on whether that's a good omen or a bad one.
The warm nights have brought out the fireflies, thousands of them, drifting over the fields like slow sparks. Colonists outside after dark will get to see them.
[lowtech] Firefly nights are here. The old folk say they're the souls of the harvest, come back to see how the fields are doing. Anyone outside after dark will see them.

li.label: bringing the ripe crops in before the hail

texts.li: The sky over the hills has gone a sick green and the wind has dropped to nothing: hail is coming. When it does, crops in the open will suffer, young ones most of all. Whoever can be spared is out bringing in what's ripe first. It won't hurt anyone and won't last long, but anyone caught outside will be miserable. (Fields under a roof are safe.)

[lowtech] The sky has turned green, the way it does before hail. Soon it will come bouncing off the roofs and stripping the leaves from everything in the fields, and young crops in the open won't all survive it. The ripe ones are being cut and carried in while there's time. It stings, but it won't hurt anyone, and it won't last long. (Fields under a roof are safe.)
[loss,lowtech] Rats got into the stores. By the time anyone noticed, they had ruined {COUNT} units of food and left droppings through the rest.
[loss,!lowtech] Big rats, the kind that will eat anything, got into the stores and chewed through or spoiled {COUNT} units of food before anyone noticed.
[mouser] Rats tried to get into the stores last night, and {PET_nameDef} caught them at it. No food was lost. {PET_nameDef} has been sitting by the storeroom door since, looking pleased.
[mining] Cutting into the rock, {A_nameDef} broke into a hollow that had been walled up long ago. Someone hid a cache there and never came back for it.
[farming] {A_nameDef}'s spade struck a box buried in the field, rotted at the corners but still shut.
[child] {A_nameDef} was digging for worms and turned up an old buried cache instead, and has been dragging people over to see it ever since.
{A_nameDef} tripped over the corner of a box sticking out of the ground and dug it up. Whoever buried it scratched three marks on the lid, and never came back to read them.
